analysis.title: NVIDIA Corp FQ3:27 (Oct) Earnings Preview: A Brave New World
key_insights: UBS expects NVDA to beat FQ3 (Oct) revenue by about $3-4B, as much as ~$111-112B, and sees FQ4 (Jan) revenue guidance near $130B against Street ~$125B, with actual revenue likely higher as Rubin ramps substantially in FQ4.

Some rack components such as rail kits are delayed. UBS compares this to prior product generations, where compute boards shipped well before rack shipments inflected. Rack shipments should inflect in CQ1:27.
FQ4 gross margin was already soft-guided to 71-72% before rebounding from FQ1, so UBS expects no margin surprises.

Investors raised concerns about NVDA's longer-term product roadmap after last week's management shake-up. UBS calls these overblown because the ecosystem pulls the roadmap along and a new CEO would be unlikely to abandon the annual product cadence. UBS still believes the denser Kyber racks are off the table.
UBS expects the company to look to the semis and tech world for a new CEO, possibly hiring from a competitor.

Biggest concerns: a possible semis correction from the mismatch between semis build plans and powered shell availability (first flagged in late September), and new scrutiny that may restrict sales into geographies such as Singapore and Malaysia.

In a worst case, geographic sales restrictions could cut up to ~10% of revenue. UBS sees no near-term effect on estimates because demand still exceeds supply, but it could matter for C2028, especially with data center readiness delays.
UBS cuts C2028E revenue/EPS from $985B/$22.08 to $885B/$20.01, a ~10% revenue cut.
C2027 was already soft-guided to growth of at least 70% Y/Y. UBS sees it possibly walked higher as a show of strength (UBSe ~80%).
Under the UBS HOLT framework, the market is assuming C2028 is the peak, no growth after, and EBITDA margins compressing ~1,500bps. UBS calls this draconian.
PT cut to $240 from $300 (12x NTM P/E on C2028E EPS of $20.01, versus 14x before). UBS keeps Buy and calls the pullback an attractive buying opportunity that may need patience.
UBS argues against giving up on the stock, as some peers did last week, ahead of January hyperscaler earnings calls where it expects capex guided above Street expectations.
UBS C2027 hyperscaler/CSP capex forecast is ~$1.76T, +69% Y/Y, with the Big Four at ~$1.13T. Spending is broadening beyond the traditional hyperscalers.

Supply: TSMC CoWoS capacity estimate unchanged at ~130k wafers per month by YE26. Industry CoWoS capacity is expected to reach ~270kwpm by YE27. HBM supply implies ~11MM NVDA units in C2027. UBS is increasingly constructive on supply, and its C2027 unit estimates reflect conservatism on deployment timing rather than supply.

Rubin checks: risk is in the timing and cadence of deployment, not full-year units. Rack forecasts remain ~80K/95K (C2026/C2027). Rail-kit shipments have shifted right, with King Slide now expecting most VR volumes in 1H27. Hon Hai says assembly bottlenecks have improved, so chip availability is the near-term constraint.
NVDA targets a ~2.5x increase in substrate capacity through 2028 across Ibiden, Unimicron and SEMCO. Unimicron's KF fab starts production in 2Q27.
UBS Evidence Lab October cloud data shows Blackwell (B200/B300) capacity being added alongside steady H100/H200 availability, which UBS reads as incremental demand rather than replacement.
UBS models gross margin at ~72-73% through at least C2027, with out-year margins depending on memory pricing and the Rubin Ultra configuration.
UBS models FCF of ~$182B in C2026 and ~$355B in C2027. NVDA plans to return at least 50% of FCF to shareholders, including ~$235B of buybacks over six quarters through FY2028.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut from $300 to $240 on a 12x NTM P/E (from 14x) applied to lower C2028E EPS of $20.01. UBS calls the pullback an attractive buying opportunity ahead of an expected FQ3 beat and higher FQ4 guide.

sector_views.rationale: AI infrastructure spending is on a steeper trajectory than investors expect, and supply (CoWoS, HBM, substrates) supports C2027 units. Risks are a correction from the powered shell gap and geographic sales scrutiny.

earnings_insights: NVDA FQ3:27 (Oct), not yet reported. UBS estimate: revenue beat of ~$3-4B versus Street, as much as ~$111-112B. UBS EPS estimate for Q3E is $2.53 versus consensus $2.48.
NVDA FQ4:27 (Jan) guidance expected by UBS at ~$130B revenue (UBS estimate) versus Street ~$125B. UBS Q4E EPS is $2.90 (from $2.95) versus consensus $2.75.
FQ4 gross margin soft-guided by the company to 71-72%, with a rebound expected from FQ1.

UBS revenue estimates: C2026 ~$418B (from ~$420B), C2027 ~$739B (from ~$744B), C2028 ~$885B (from ~$985B per summary text). UBS Data Center revenue estimates are ~$391B and ~$710B for C2026 and C2027.
UBS product mix estimate for C2026: 67% Blackwell Ultra, 26% Rubin, 6% Blackwell, 1% Hopper. C2027: ~81% Rubin, 14% Rubin Ultra, 5% Blackwell.
UBS GPU unit estimates are ~8.2MM in C2026 (from 8.1MM) and ~8.4MM in C2027 (unchanged). Total chip volumes including CPUs and LPUs are ~9.8MM and ~14.3MM.

trade_ideas.description: Buy NVDA (UBS Buy rating, 12-month PT $240) on weakness ahead of the FQ3 print and January hyperscaler earnings calls
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS expects a revenue beat, higher FQ4 guidance and above-Street hyperscaler capex guidance, while HOLT-implied valuation prices in a C2028 peak.
trade_ideas.risk: Semis correction from the powered shell gap, sales restrictions into Singapore/Malaysia, and CEO transition uncertainty.

risk_factors: Mismatch between semis build plans and powered shell availability could cause a semis correction.
Scrutiny restricting sales into Singapore and Malaysia, worst case up to ~10% of revenue.
Delays in data center readiness and availability, relevant for C2028.
Management shake-up and CEO search, with roadmap concerns.
Rubin ramp more back-end loaded, with rail-kit delays shifting volume to 1H27.
Out-year gross margins depend on memory pricing and Rubin Ultra configuration.
Competition from purpose-built alternatives that look competitive on raw $/FLOP.
charts_described: Cloud accelerator study (Figure 32): UBS reads October data as continued B200/B300 build-out alongside steady H100/H200 availability across clouds.
vol_and_positioning: UBS says some peers gave up on the stock last week after the management shake-up, and that near-term damage to the stock has been done.
The stock is at US$162.85, the bottom of its 52-week range of US$239.24-162.85.
geopolitical: New scrutiny may restrict some NVDA sales into geographies such as Singapore and Malaysia. UBS estimates a worst case of up to ~10% of revenue.
Read-through from Trump-Xi talks to semis appears in the list of recent UBS research (SemiBytes, 08/31/26).

tension_points.bull_case: UBS says the ecosystem pulls the roadmap along and a new CEO is unlikely to risk competitive standing by dropping the annual product cadence.
tension_points.bear_case: Many investors worry about NVDA's longer-term product roadmap after the management shake-up, and some peers have given up on the stock.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A new CEO moving away from the annual product cadence, or the denser Kyber racks staying on the roadmap.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler/CSP capex of ~$1.76T in C2027 (+69% Y/Y) with broadening participation, and UBS expects January capex guidance above Street.
tension_points.bear_case: Powered shell availability mismatch, data center readiness delays and possible geographic sales restrictions (up to ~10% of revenue) could hit C2028.
tension_points.what_invalidates: January hyperscaler earnings calls guiding capex at or below current Street expectations.
